correctness.rationale: Exact bijection from primitive Euclid parameters to odd coprime u<v verifies domain and normalization; primitive odd leg uv is kth-power-free iff both factors are. At odd p the forbidden classes are both divisible by p or one divisible by p^k with the other a p-unit; these are disjoint and yield the local factor. Finite-prime CRT gives density in the circular sector; union bounds for primes above z are O_k(X/z+sqrt(X)log X), so cutoff removal is rigorous for fixed k>=2. The sector area pi X/4, parity factor 1/4, and odd-prime zeta factor 8/pi^2 give the claimed coefficient. Independent exact enumerators agreed through X=10^6 at k=2,3,4; those experiments are not substituted for the infinite proof. Limitation: o_k(X) only.

value.rationale: The odd leg is a canonical arithmetic coordinate of every primitive Pythagorean triangle, unlike the even leg which is always a multiple of four. Determining what fraction of all primitive triangles have a squarefree or, more generally, kth-power-free odd leg answers a naturally motivated distribution problem. The exact positive Euler product records the nontrivial coupling of coprimality with local kth-power restrictions, providing a concrete unbounded invariant, not a lookup table or a renaming of a fixed sample. An entirely elementary proof does not by itself invalidate this natural classification.
